output:
To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: Draft — please do not enter 43 or attempt propping

Mick, please do not go into 43 at 9, with your lad or anyone else, to put props in or inspect the loft. Priya, please do not hand over a key for this. I know the offer is well meant, but underneath a holed roof with a loose chimney above is the worst place to stand.

I’m a chartered structural engineer with IStructE, but I’m speaking here only as a neighbour who looked from the opposite pavement at about 7 this morning. This is not a commission or a structural inspection, and I have no professional indemnity cover for informal advice. I cannot certify either house as safe.

Part of 41’s stack is still standing and appears to lean towards 43, with visibly deteriorated mortar at its base. At 43 I could see the roof hole, a stepped crack above the bay and apparent movement at the bay head. Loose slates along the gutter line at 43 and 45 are directly above the pavement. More strong gusts are forecast this afternoon.

There may be debris loading the floors inside. We do not know how loads are now being carried through the damaged building. Putting Acrows under a ceiling without establishing that could make matters worse. An inspection from inside the loft is not a safe alternative.

JoJo, your cousin’s general point about Victorian terraces being robust is fair, but this particular terrace has suffered significant damage.

Priya: I cannot say Mrs Doherty is safe because 45 looks undamaged from the front; I could not see the shared wall. It is not my decision whether she leaves, but I would not sleep in her front room tonight. Staying with family until 45 has been checked would be the safer choice.

Please use the other side of the road, especially for the school run, until the council has assessed the danger and advised on access. Garden tape does not mean the footway is safe. The council already knows, but the pavement remains open: please report that and the loose material urgently through the main council number, asking for out-of-hours dangerous structures. If anything is falling or collapse appears imminent, call 999 and keep clear.
